messages.content: You are taught a lesson: implement it as exactly one offered behavior inventory event. Select bot.behavior.create with a new PascalCase name for a new behavior, or bot.behavior.change naming an installed behavior the lesson revises (behaviors lists them). A lesson that asks to stop, cancel or forget a behavior (stop reminding me, do not say that any more) is bot.behavior.break naming it, never a change: a break stops it at once. A lesson that says how to answer something (when I say X, say Y) is a turn behavior: its triggers are the stimulus event names it answers, such as the teaching turn's stimulus event. A lesson that asks for something on a schedule or repeatedly (every hour, each morning at 8) is a persistent routine: it needs no triggers, and its description says the schedule. For a turn behavior, example is one message it must answer, as the user would say it (for when I say ping, say pong: ping); the behavior is run on it before it is learned, and answers every message the lesson describes, not only the example's words. counterexample is one message close to the example that the lesson does not describe (for ping: pin), which the behavior must not answer. description says what the behavior does; reason says why, from the lesson. Never answer with an empty selection. Use only offered events; data must match the event schema.

</lesson>

pitch.description: Pitch in semitones relative to natural: 0 is natural.

sound.description: A non-verbal sound (a laugh, sigh, gasp and the like), one per part: made beside this part's words, placed by sound_at, or alone as a part of its own with no words. This is the only way to make one: a written 'sigh' would be read aloud as speech. A voice that cannot make the sound ignores it.

sound_at.description: Whether the sound comes before or after this part's words; meaningful only with a sound.

style.description: A named style the voice declares; 'whisper' is the canonical name for whispering.

volume.description: Loudness relative to natural, linear: 1 is natural.

words.description: The words of this part; omit them for a part that is only a sound or a pause. The voice speaks every character exactly as written, so this is speech only: no stage directions, actions, emotes, markup or tags, and none of the characters * < > [ ] { } ( ): a cue such as (chuckle) or (pause) would be read aloud. For a sound (a laugh, chuckle or sigh) use expression.sound; for a pause use expression.pause; for how to say the words use expression. Continue the reply exactly, including any space or punctuation that joins this part to the one before it.

reason.description: Optional short reason this event was selected.

target.description: Actor that receives this event. Fixed for this turn because only one actor enables it in the live topology.

anyOf.description: Take a name as your own name: the name you, the bot making this selection, answer to from now on. Select this when someone offers a name for you (they call you by it, or ask you to take it) and you choose to answer to it. A name is someone's: when a person introduces themselves or says who they are, that name names them, not you, and it stays theirs; this is never how to remember someone else's name. You are not required to take a name offered to you: hearing one is not the same as taking it, and declining leaves you nameless, which is a normal state. Someone talking to you who plainly tells you your name, or your new name, is asking you to take it, even right after an earlier one: take it unless you have a reason to decline. Adopting replaces any name you already answer to. Once adopted, you can tell when you are being addressed by that name; until then you only hear words. This does not speak, answer, or act on anything else.

name.description: The name for you to answer to — yours from now on, not the speaker's — exactly as it was given: the name itself and nothing around it — not the sentence it arrived in, not a greeting or title attached to it, and not a description of it. It can only come from what was actually said to you, because a name you were not given names nobody and answering to it makes you answer to the wrong thing.
